citation: Bilal MA, Ul Islam I, Idrees S, Qasim M, Khan MJ, Khan J, et al. Dataset-centric evaluation of federated intrusion detection models in IoT networks. Scientific Reports 16:2683, 2026. doi:10.1038/s41598-025-32567-w

A1.evidence: Methodology: 'each dataset was split among multiple clients ... (Table 2)'; 'Per client, we fit a standard scaler on the training split' — how train/test splits were formed is not stated (only a 'stratified 90/10 split' for validation in ablations).

A2.evidence: Methodology: LSTM inputs 'fed as a length-1 sequence–treating each flow as one timestep'.

A3.evidence: Methodology: 'z-score normalization (fit on training split only); in cross-dataset tests the source scaler is applied to the target.'

A4.evidence: 'typically 50 rounds for single-dataset cases and up to 100 for the combined one'; 'training locally for 5 epochs with mini-batches of 128 samples.'

A5.evidence: 'These settings were kept consistent across algorithms to fairly compare FedAvg, FedProx, and FedNova.'

A6.evidence: FedAvg, FedProx, FedNova with LSTM/Transformer run by the authors (Tables 5-9); no comparison table with numbers from other papers.

A7.evidence: Metrics: 'Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score, AUC' and confusion matrix; no MCC/balanced accuracy/G-mean.

A8.evidence: Clients formed by natural grouping: 'Edge-IIoTset ... 6 clients by device/application; CIC-IoT2023 into 10 clients by device group; TII-SSRC-23 into 5 clients by stratified random flows' — natural/IID splits only, no synthetic non-IID partition.

A9.evidence: Only fixed seeds stated ('Global seed 42 with dataset seeds Edge=1729, CIC=2023, TII=1103'); no multiple runs, dispersion or tests.

A10.evidence: Cross-dataset design: 'train on one dataset and test on another'; 'For each source model we apply the source-fitted scaler to the target features'; 'Metrics are macro-averaged on the target test set.'

A11.evidence: Data availability lists dataset links only; 'Exact client indices and split files are provided in the supplementary package' — no code link.

notes: Bash egress to nature.com blocked; read through web text extraction (several targeted passes). No centralized baseline results table found despite abstract claim 'federated models approach centralized performance in-domain'. A8: the paper calls its device-based clients 'non-IID', but per protocol a device/application grouping is a natural split, so coded no; flag if second coder reads it otherwise. A sensitivity sweep reports macro-F1 changes '≤ ±0.5 percentage points' across hyperparameters, not repeated runs.
